name: Adai Dosa (Lentil Dosa)
instructions: Soak 40 g of Rice, 20 g of Chana Dal, and 20 g of Toor Dal in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain the soaked ingredients and transfer them to a blender.
Add 1 piece of Red Chilli and 5 pieces of Curry Leaves to the blender.
Blend the mixture into a smooth batter, adding a little water if necessary to achieve a pourable consistency.
Heat a non-stick skillet or tawa over medium heat and lightly grease it with oil.
Pour a ladleful of the batter onto the skillet and spread it into a circular shape.
Cook the dosa for about 2-3 minutes until the edges start to lift and the bottom is golden brown.
Flip the dosa and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the other side is cooked through.
Repeat the process with the remaining batter, greasing the skillet as needed.
Serve the Adai Dosa hot with chutney or sambar for breakfast.

name: Banana Jowar Pancake
instructions: In a mixing bowl, mash the 1 piece of banana until smooth.
Add 50 g of Jowar Flour, 1 piece of egg, and 0.25 tsp of cinnamon powder to the mashed banana.
Mix all the ingredients together until you have a smooth batter.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease it if necessary.
Pour a ladleful of the batter onto the skillet, forming a pancake.
Cook for about 2-3 minutes on one side until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Repeat the process with the remaining batter, adjusting the heat as needed.
Serve the pancakes warm for breakfast.

name: Curd Poha with Pomegranate
instructions: Rinse 50 g of flattened rice in water and drain it well, allowing it to soften for about 10 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine the softened flattened rice with 80 g of low-fat curd.
Add 50 g of pomegranate seeds to the mixture for a burst of flavor and texture.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp of cumin seeds over the mixture and gently fold all the ingredients together until well combined.
Let the mixture sit for a few minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve the curd poha in a bowl, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds if desired.

name: Egg Salad with Whole Wheat Toast
instructions: Boil 2 pieces of egg in water for about 10 minutes until hard-boiled.
Once cooked, remove the eggs from the water and let them cool before peeling.
While the eggs are cooling, slice 50g of cucumber into small pieces.
In a bowl, chop the peeled eggs and add the sliced cucumber.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon into the bowl with the eggs and cucumber.
Drizzle 1 tsp of olive oil over the mixture and gently stir to combine all ingredients.
Toast 2 pieces of whole wheat bread until golden brown.
Serve the egg salad on top of the toasted whole wheat bread.

name: Grilled Paneer Sandwich with Mint Chutney
instructions: Start by preparing the mint chutney. In a blender, combine 10 g of mint leaves and 10 g of coriander leaves with a little water to create a smooth paste.
Take 60 g of low-fat paneer and slice it into thin pieces.
Toast 2 pieces of whole wheat bread on a grill or in a toaster until golden brown.
Spread the prepared mint chutney evenly on one side of each slice of toasted bread.
Layer the sliced paneer on top of the chutney on one slice of bread.
Top with the other slice of bread, chutney side down, to form a sandwich.
Grill the sandwich on medium heat for about 2-3 minutes on each side until the paneer is warm and the bread is crispy.
Remove the sandwich from the grill, cut it in half, and serve immediately for breakfast.

name: Methi Handvo (Baked)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a mixing bowl, combine 50 g of rice flour and 20 g of toor dal.
Finely chop 20 g of fenugreek leaves and add them to the flour and dal mixture.
Stir in 40 g of low-fat curd until the mixture is well combined.
Add water as needed to achieve a smooth batter consistency.
Grease a baking dish and pour the batter into it, spreading it evenly.
Sprinkle 1 tsp of sesame seeds on top of the batter.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 30-35 minutes or until golden brown.
Once baked, allow it to cool slightly before cutting into pieces and serving for breakfast.

name: Methi Thepla with Curd
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 60 g of whole wheat flour and 30 g of finely chopped fenugreek leaves.
Add 50 g of low-fat curd to the flour and fenugreek mixture, and knead into a soft dough.
Let the dough rest for about 10 minutes, covered with a damp cloth.
Divide the dough into small balls, and roll each ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and add 1 tsp of oil.
Place the rolled thepla on the skillet and cook for about 1-2 minutes on each side until golden brown, adding a little oil if needed.
Remove the thepla from the skillet and keep it warm in a container.
Serve the methi thepla hot with a side of low-fat curd.

name: Oats Idli
instructions: Dry roast 50 g of oats in a pan until they turn slightly golden and aromatic, then let them cool.
Grind the roasted oats into a fine powder and transfer it to a mixing bowl.
Add 30 g of semolina to the bowl with the ground oats.
In a separate bowl, mix 50 g of low-fat curd with water to achieve a smooth consistency, then add it to the oats and semolina mixture.
Stir the mixture well until all ingredients are combined and let it rest for about 15 minutes.
In a small pan, heat a teaspoon of oil and add 0.5 tsp of mustard seeds; let them splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves to the pan and sauté for a few seconds, then pour this tempering into the idli batter and mix well.
Grease the idli molds and pour the batter into them, filling each mold about three-quarters full.
Steam the idlis in a steamer for about 10-12 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Remove the idlis from the molds and serve hot with chutney or sambar for breakfast.

name: Ragi Dosa with Coconut Chutney
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 60 g of Ragi Flour and 20 g of Rice Flour.
Add enough water to the flour mixture to form a smooth batter, and let it rest for 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the coconut chutney by grinding 30 g of Coconut, 1 piece of Green Chilli, and 5 pieces of Curry Leaves together with a little water until smooth.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease it.
Pour a ladleful of the rested batter onto the skillet and spread it into a thin circle.
Cook the dosa for about 2-3 minutes until the edges lift and the bottom is golden brown.
Flip the dosa and cook for another minute on the other side.
Serve the hot ragi dosa with the prepared coconut chutney on the side.

name: Ragi Malt with Milk and Jaggery
instructions: In a bowl, mix 40 g of Ragi Flour with a little water to form a smooth paste.
In a saucepan, heat 200 ml of Milk over medium heat until it begins to simmer.
Gradually add the Ragi Flour paste to the simmering Milk, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cook the mixture for about 5-7 minutes, stirring until it thickens to a desired consistency.
Add 15 g of Jaggery to the mixture and stir until it completely dissolves.
Finally, add 0.25 tsp of Cardamom and mix well.
Serve the Ragi Malt warm in a bowl for breakfast.

name: Rava Idli with Coconut Chutney
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 60 g of semolina and 50 g of low-fat curd, mixing well to form a batter.
Let the batter rest for about 15 minutes to allow the semolina to absorb moisture.
Meanwhile, prepare the coconut chutney by grinding 30 g of coconut with a little water until smooth.
In a small pan, heat a teaspoon of oil and add 0.5 tsp of mustard seeds, allowing them to splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves to the pan and sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Combine the tempered mustard seeds and curry leaves with the ground coconut chutney, mixing well.
After the resting period, pour the batter into idli molds and steam for about 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
Serve the rava idlis hot with the coconut chutney on the side.

name: Sooji Sheera with Jaggery
instructions: In a pan, heat 2 teaspoons of ghee over medium heat until melted.
Add 40 grams of semolina to the pan and roast it, stirring continuously, until it turns golden brown and fragrant.
In a separate bowl, dissolve 20 grams of jaggery in a small amount of warm water to create a syrup.
Once the semolina is roasted, slowly pour the jaggery syrup into the pan while stirring to combine.
Add 0.25 teaspoons of cardamom to the mixture and stir well.
Continue to cook for a few minutes until the mixture thickens and the semolina absorbs the syrup.
Remove from heat and let it sit for a minute before serving.
Serve the Sooji Sheera warm, garnished with additional ghee if desired.

name: Tomato Carrot Uttapam
instructions: Soak 50 g of rice and 20 g of urad dal in water for about 4-6 hours or overnight.
Drain the soaked rice and urad dal, then blend them together with a little water to form a smooth batter.
Transfer the batter to a bowl and let it ferment for 6-8 hours in a warm place.
Once fermented, finely chop 40 g of tomato, 30 g of carrot, and 5 pieces of curry leaves.
Gently fold the chopped tomato, carrot, and curry leaves into the fermented batter.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease it.
Pour a ladleful of the batter onto the skillet, spreading it into a thick pancake shape.
Cook for about 3-4 minutes on one side until golden brown, then flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve the tomato carrot uttapam hot with chutney or sambar for breakfast.

name: Vegetable Daliya
instructions: Heat 1 tsp of ghee in a pan over medium heat.
Add 0.5 tsp of cumin seeds to the ghee and sauté until they start to crackle.
Finely chop the 30 g of carrot and add it to the pan, cooking for about 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add 30 g of green peas to the pan and stir for another minute.
Add 60 g of broken wheat to the pan and mix well with the vegetables.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let it simmer for about 15 minutes until the broken wheat is cooked and the water is absorbed.
Fluff the daliya with a fork and serve hot for breakfast.

name: Vegetable Upma
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of ghee in a pan over medium heat.
Add 0.5 teaspoon of mustard seeds to the ghee and let them splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves to the pan and sauté for a few seconds.
Finely chop the 30 grams of carrot and add it to the pan, cooking until slightly softened.
Add 30 grams of green peas to the pan and stir for a minute.
Add 60 grams of semolina to the pan and roast it for about 2-3 minutes until it turns light golden.
Pour in 1.5 cups of water and stir well to avoid lumps.
Cook the mixture on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the water is absorbed and the semolina is cooked through.
Remove from heat and let it sit covered for a couple of minutes before serving.

name: Baked Aloo Chaat
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash and peel the 150 g of potato, then cut it into small cubes.
Place the potato cubes on a baking tray and bake in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes, or until they are golden and crispy.
Once the potatoes are baked, remove them from the oven and let them cool slightly.
In a mixing bowl, combine the baked potatoes with 0.5 tsp of chaat masala.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon over the potatoes and mix well.
Finely chop 2 tbsp of coriander leaves and add them to the potato mixture, stirring to combine.
Serve the baked aloo chaat warm, garnished with additional coriander leaves if desired.

name: Corn Pomegranate Bhutta Chaat
instructions: Boil 100 g of sweet corn in water for about 5-7 minutes until tender, then drain and let cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the boiled sweet corn and 50 g of pomegranate seeds.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon over the corn and pomegranate mixture.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp of chaat masala over the mixture and toss gently to combine all the ingredients.
Serve the Corn Pomegranate Bhutta Chaat in a bowl, garnished with additional pomegranate seeds if desired.

name: Dahi Bhalla (Moong Dal)
instructions: Soak 50 g of Moong Dal in water for about 4-5 hours until it softens.
Drain the soaked Moong Dal and blend it into a smooth batter, adding a little water if necessary.
In a mixing bowl, combine the Moong Dal batter with 0.5 tsp of Cumin Powder and mix well.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and lightly grease it.
Drop spoonfuls of the Moong Dal batter onto the pan to form small fritters and cook until golden brown on both sides.
Once cooked, remove the fritters and let them cool on a paper towel to absorb excess oil.
In a serving bowl, place the fritters and pour 100 g of Low-Fat Curd over them.
Garnish with 2 tbsp of chopped Coriander Leaves for added flavor and freshness.
Serve immediately as a delicious brunch dish.

name: Fruit Chaat with Chaat Masala
instructions: Chop the 0.5 piece of apple into small cubes.
Slice the 0.5 piece of banana into thin rounds.
In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped apple and sliced banana.
Add 50 g of pomegranate seeds to the bowl with the fruits.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp of chaat masala over the fruit mixture.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until well combined.
Serve the fruit chaat in a bowl as a refreshing brunch option.

name: Grilled Vegetable Sandwich
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium heat.
Slice the cucumber, tomato, and bell pepper into thin strips.
Grill the bell pepper strips for about 3-4 minutes until they are tender and have grill marks.
Toast the whole wheat bread pieces on the grill for 1-2 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Layer the grilled bell pepper, cucumber, and tomato slices on one piece of toasted bread.
Sprinkle the mint leaves over the vegetables for added flavor.
Top with the second piece of toasted bread to complete the sandwich.
Cut the sandwich in half and serve immediately for brunch.

name: Roasted Makhana Trail Mix
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Spread the 20 g of Makhana evenly on a baking sheet.
Add 10 g of Almonds to the baking sheet with the Makhana.
Include 10 g of Pumpkin Seeds on the baking sheet as well.
Roast the mixture in the oven for about 10-12 minutes, stirring halfway through to ensure even roasting.
Once roasted, remove the baking sheet from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes.
After cooling, mix in 10 g of Dried Cranberries with the roasted nuts and seeds.
Serve the Roasted Makhana Trail Mix in a bowl for a healthy brunch snack.

name: Roasted Puffed Rice with Peanuts
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a mixing bowl, combine 40 g of puffed rice and 15 g of peanuts.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves and 0.25 tsp of turmeric powder to the mixture.
Toss all the ingredients together until the puffed rice and peanuts are evenly coated with the turmeric and curry leaves.
Spread the mixture evenly on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for about 10-12 minutes, or until the peanuts are golden and fragrant.
Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.
Serve the roasted puffed rice with peanuts as a crunchy brunch snack.

name: Sweet Potato Chaat
instructions: Peel and dice the 150 g of sweet potato into small cubes.
Boil the diced sweet potato in water for about 10-15 minutes until tender, then drain and let cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled sweet potato with 0.5 tsp of chaat masala.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon over the sweet potato mixture.
Finely chop 2 tbsp of coriander leaves and add them to the bowl.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until well mixed.
Serve the sweet potato chaat in a bowl, garnished with extra coriander leaves if desired.

name: Til Jaggery Ladoo
instructions: In a pan, heat 1 tsp of ghee over low flame until melted.
Add 30 g of sesame seeds to the pan and roast them gently, stirring continuously until they turn golden brown and fragrant.
Once the sesame seeds are roasted, remove the pan from heat and let it cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, break 20 g of jaggery into small pieces.
Add the jaggery to the warm sesame seeds and mix well until the jaggery melts and combines with the seeds.
Once the mixture is cool enough to handle, grease your hands with a little ghee.
Take small portions of the mixture and shape them into round ladoos.
Place the formed ladoos on a plate and let them cool completely before serving.

name: Watermelon Cucumber Salad
instructions: Start by cutting the 150 g of watermelon into bite-sized cubes and place them in a mixing bowl.
Next, slice the 80 g of cucumber into thin rounds and add them to the bowl with the watermelon.
Finely chop the 5 g of mint leaves and sprinkle them over the watermelon and cucumber in the bowl.
Squeeze the juice from half a lemon (0.5 piece) over the salad to add a refreshing tang.
Gently toss all the ingredients together to combine the flavors evenly.
Serve the watermelon cucumber salad chilled, garnished with a few extra mint leaves if desired.

name: Bajra Khichdi with Ghee
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Bajra and 30 g of Moong Dal under running water until the water runs clear.
Soak the Bajra and Moong Dal in water for about 30 minutes to soften them.
In a pressure cooker, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat.
Add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds to the hot Ghee and sauté until they crackle.
Finely chop 2 g of Ginger and add it to the cooker, sautéing for a minute until fragrant.
Drain the soaked Bajra and Moong Dal, then add them to the cooker and stir well to combine with the spices.
Add 2 cups of water to the mixture, stir, and close the pressure cooker lid.
Cook on high heat until the first whistle, then reduce the heat and cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Once done, allow the pressure to release naturally, then open the lid and fluff the Khichdi with a fork before serving.

name: Bharwan Shimla Mirch with Chapati
instructions: Wash and deseed the 150 g of bell pepper, then cut them in half to create pockets for stuffing.
Boil the 60 g of potato until tender, then peel and mash it in a bowl.
In the bowl with the mashed potato, add 0.5 tsp of cumin seeds and 0.5 tsp of turmeric powder, mixing well to combine the flavors.
Stuff each half of the bell pepper with the potato mixture, pressing it in firmly.
In a separate bowl, mix 80 g of whole wheat flour with water to form a smooth dough for the chapati.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook each chapati for about 1-2 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Serve the stuffed bell peppers alongside the freshly made chapatis for dinner.

name: Chicken Vegetable Soup
instructions: Start by dicing the 80 g of Chicken Breast into small pieces.
Peel and slice the 40 g of Carrot into thin rounds.
Trim and cut the 40 g of Green Beans into bite-sized pieces.
In a pot, add the diced Chicken Breast and sauté over medium heat until lightly browned.
Add the sliced Carrot and Green Beans to the pot, stirring to combine.
Grate the 2 g of Ginger and add it to the pot, mixing well with the other ingredients.
Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let the soup simmer for about 20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Season the soup with 0.25 tsp of Black Pepper before serving hot.

name: Grilled Fish with Steamed Vegetables
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Drizzle 1 teaspoon of olive oil over the 120 g of fish, ensuring it is evenly coated.
Season the fish with salt and pepper to taste, if desired.
Place the fish on the preheated grill and cook for about 4-5 minutes on each side, or until it flakes easily with a fork.
While the fish is grilling, prepare the vegetables by cutting the 60 g of broccoli and 40 g of carrot into bite-sized pieces.
Steam the broccoli and carrot together for about 5-7 minutes, or until they are tender but still crisp.
Once the fish is cooked, remove it from the grill and squeeze the juice of half a lemon over it for added flavor.
Serve the grilled fish alongside the steamed broccoli and carrot for a healthy dinner.

name: Grilled Paneer Tikka (Lemon Marinade)
instructions: Cut the 100 g of Low-Fat Paneer into cubes and set aside.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of Lemon into a bowl.
Grate 5 g of Ginger and add it to the bowl with the lemon juice.
Add 0.25 tsp of Black Pepper to the marinade and mix well.
Chop 50 g of Bell Pepper into bite-sized pieces and add them to the marinade.
Add the paneer cubes to the marinade, ensuring they are well coated, and let them marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Skewer the marinated paneer and bell pepper pieces alternately onto skewers.
Grill the skewers for about 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally until the paneer is golden and slightly charred.
Serve the grilled paneer tikka hot, garnished with lemon wedges.

name: Lauki Sabji with Moong Dal and Rice
instructions: Rinse the 40 g of Moong Dal thoroughly under running water and soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
Peel and chop the 100 g of Doodhi (Bottle Gourd) into small cubes.
In a pot, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds, allowing them to splutter.
Add the chopped Doodhi to the pot and sauté for about 5 minutes until it begins to soften.
Drain the soaked Moong Dal and add it to the pot, stirring well to combine with the Doodhi.
Pour in enough water to cover the mixture and bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer until the Moong Dal is cooked, about 15-20 minutes.
While the sabji is cooking, rinse the 60 g of Rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a separate pot, add the rinsed Rice and double the amount of water, then bring it to a boil, reduce the heat, cover, and cook for about 15 minutes until the Rice is fluffy and water is absorbed.
Once both the Lauki Sabji and Rice are ready, serve the sabji hot alongside the Rice for dinner.

name: Light Dal Makhani
instructions: Soak 60 g of Urad Dal and 20 g of Red Kidney Beans in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain the soaked dal and beans, then rinse them under cold water.
In a pressure cooker, add the soaked Urad Dal and Red Kidney Beans along with 2 cups of water.
Cook on high heat until the pressure builds, then reduce to low heat and cook for about 15-20 minutes.
Once cooked, release the pressure and open the lid, then mash the dal and beans slightly for a creamy texture.
In a pan, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat, then add 5 g of finely chopped Ginger and sauté until fragrant.
Add 60 g of chopped Tomato to the pan and cook until it softens and blends with the ginger.
Combine the cooked dal and beans with the tomato-ginger mixture, stirring well to combine.
Simmer the mixture for an additional 5-10 minutes, adjusting the consistency with water if needed.
Serve the Light Dal Makhani hot, garnished with a drizzle of ghee if desired.

name: Masoor Dal with Rice and Ghee
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Masoor Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Masoor Dal along with 2 cups of water and bring it to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let the dal simmer for about 20 minutes, or until it is soft and fully cooked.
In a separate pot, rinse 80 g of Rice under cold water and then add it to 1.5 cups of boiling water.
Cover the pot and cook the rice on low heat for about 15 minutes, or until all the water is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
In a small pan, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds.
Sauté the cumin seeds until they are fragrant, then pour the ghee and cumin mixture over the cooked Masoor Dal.
Serve the Masoor Dal hot alongside the fluffy Rice on a plate, drizzling any remaining ghee over the rice if desired.

name: Methi Dal with Jowar Bhakri
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Moong Dal under running water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Moong Dal along with 2 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until the dal is soft, approximately 20 minutes.
While the dal is cooking, wash and chop 40 g of Fenugreek Leaves finely.
In a small pan, heat a teaspoon of oil and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds. Sauté until they start to crackle.
Add the chopped Fenugreek Leaves and 2 pieces of minced Garlic to the pan, and cook for about 3-4 minutes until the leaves wilt.
Once the dal is cooked, stir in the sautéed fenugreek mixture and season with salt to taste. Let it simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine 80 g of Jowar Flour with water to form a smooth dough. Divide the dough into small balls.
Roll each ball into a flat disc using a rolling pin, dusting with additional jowar flour as needed.
Heat a tava or skillet over medium heat and cook each bhakri for about 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve the Methi Dal hot with the freshly made Jowar Bhakri for dinner.

name: Palak Dal with Rice
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Toor Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Toor Dal with 2 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the dal is soft.
While the dal is cooking, rinse 80 g of Rice under cold water and cook it in a separate pot with 1.5 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy.
In a pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds. Sauté until they start to crackle.
Mince 2 pieces of Garlic and add them to the pan, cooking until they are golden brown.
Wash and chop 60 g of Spinach, then add it to the pan with the garlic and cumin. Sauté until the spinach wilts down.
Once the Toor Dal is cooked, add the sautéed spinach mixture to the dal and stir well. Cook for an additional 5 minutes to combine the flavors.
Serve the Palak Dal hot alongside the cooked Rice on a plate.

name: Tofu Bhurji with Chapati
instructions: Start by crumbling 100 g of tofu into a bowl and set it aside.
Finely chop 40 g of onion and 40 g of tomato.
In a pan, heat a little oil over medium heat and add the chopped onion, sautéing until it becomes translucent.
Add the chopped tomato to the pan and cook until it softens, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in 0.5 tsp of turmeric powder and mix well with the onion and tomato.
Add the crumbled tofu to the pan and cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally to combine all the flavors.
While the tofu bhurji is cooking, prepare the chapati by mixing 80 g of whole wheat flour with water to form a soft dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Cook each chapati on a hot skillet for about 1-2 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Serve the tofu bhurji hot with the freshly made chapati.

name: Tomato Basil Soup with Grilled Paneer
instructions: Begin by finely chopping the 120g of tomatoes and set them aside.
In a pot, add the chopped tomatoes along with 2 pieces of minced garlic.
Cook the mixture over medium heat until the tomatoes soften and release their juices, about 10 minutes.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, blend the mixture until smooth and return it to the pot.
Add 5g of fresh basil leaves to the blended tomato soup and let it simmer for another 5 minutes.
While the soup simmers, cut the 50g of low-fat paneer into cubes.
In a separate pan, grill the paneer cubes until they are golden brown on all sides.
Serve the hot tomato basil soup in bowls, topped with the grilled paneer cubes.
Garnish with additional basil leaves if desired and enjoy your dinner.

name: Turai Sabji with Chapati
instructions: Peel and chop the 150 g of Ridge Gourd into small pieces.
Finely chop the 40 g of Onion.
In a pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds, allowing them to sizzle.
Add the chopped Onion to the pan and sauté until it turns translucent.
Stir in the chopped Ridge Gourd and cook for about 5 minutes until it softens.
Add 0.5 tsp of Turmeric Powder and mix well, cooking for an additional 2-3 minutes.
In a separate bowl, combine 80 g of Whole Wheat Flour with water to knead into a soft dough for the Chapati.
Divide the dough into small balls, roll them out into thin circles, and cook on a hot griddle until golden brown on both sides.
Serve the Turai Sabji hot with the freshly made Chapati for dinner.

name: Vegetable Jowar Khichdi
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Jowar and 30 g of Moong Dal under running water until the water runs clear.
Soak the rinsed Jowar and Moong Dal in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pressure cooker, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat.
Add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds to the hot Ghee and sauté until they start to crackle.
Drain the soaked Jowar and Moong Dal, then add them to the pressure cooker along with 80 g of Mixed Vegetables.
Stir everything together and sauté for a couple of minutes to combine the flavors.
Add enough water to cover the mixture, then close the lid of the pressure cooker.
Cook on high heat for 2 whistles, then reduce the heat and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, then open the lid and fluff the Khichdi with a fork before serving.

name: Vegetable Masala Khichdi
instructions: Rinse 50 g of rice and 40 g of moong dal under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a pot, heat 1 tsp of ghee over medium heat.
Add the rinsed moong dal to the pot and sauté for 2-3 minutes until it turns slightly golden.
Stir in 80 g of mixed vegetables and sauté for another 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice to the pot along with 0.5 tsp of turmeric powder and mix well.
Pour in enough water to cover the mixture, about 3 cups, and bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes until the rice and dal are cooked and the water is absorbed.
Fluff the khichdi with a fork and serve hot for dinner.

name: Vegetable Soup with Whole Wheat Toast
instructions: Chop the ginger into small pieces and set aside.
In a pot, add the mixed vegetables and enough water to cover them, then bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat and add the chopped ginger and black pepper.
Simmer the soup for about 15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
While the soup is simmering, toast the whole wheat bread until golden brown.
Serve the vegetable soup hot in a bowl, accompanied by the toasted whole wheat bread on the side.

name: Adrak Chai (Ginger Tea)
instructions: In a saucepan, combine 150 ml of water and 1 tsp of grated ginger.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat.
Once boiling, add 1 tsp of black tea leaves and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes.
After simmering, add 100 ml of milk to the saucepan.
Stir the mixture and bring it back to a gentle boil.
Once it reaches a boil, remove the saucepan from heat.
Strain the tea into a cup to remove the ginger and tea leaves.
Serve the Adrak Chai hot as an evening snack.

name: Baked Besan Pakora
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
In a mixing bowl, combine 50 g of chickpea flour (besan) with 0.25 tsp of ajwain.
Finely chop 40 g of onion and add it to the bowl.
Wash and chop 20 g of spinach, then mix it into the batter.
Add water gradually to the mixture until you achieve a thick batter consistency.
Grease a baking tray with 1 tsp of oil.
Spoon the batter onto the greased tray, forming small fritters.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before serving as an evening snack.

name: Baked Vegetable Cutlet
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Boil the 80g of potato until tender, then mash it in a bowl.
Grate the 40g of carrot and add it to the mashed potato.
Add 40g of green peas to the mixture, along with 20g of chickpea flour (besan) and 0.5 tsp of garam masala.
Mix all the ingredients thoroughly until well combined.
Shape the mixture into cutlet forms and place them on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake the cutlets in the preheated oven for about 20-25 minutes, or until they are golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let them cool slightly before serving as an evening snack.

name: Coconut Jaggery Ladoo
instructions: Grate 40 g of coconut and set it aside.
In a pan, add the grated coconut and heat it on low flame for a few minutes until it becomes slightly dry.
Add 20 g of jaggery to the pan and mix well with the coconut until the jaggery melts completely.
Sprinkle 0.25 tsp of cardamom into the mixture and stir well to combine all the flavors.
Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly until it is manageable.
Once cool enough to handle, take small portions of the mixture and shape them into round ladoos.
Place the ladoos on a plate and allow them to cool completely before serving as an evening snack.

name: Date and Seed Energy Balls
instructions: In a food processor, combine 40g of dates, 10g of pumpkin seeds, 10g of sunflower seeds, and 10g of coconut.
Pulse the mixture until it forms a sticky, cohesive dough.
Once the mixture is ready, take small portions and roll them into bite-sized balls.
Place the energy balls on a plate or tray lined with parchment paper.
Refrigerate the energy balls for at least 30 minutes to firm up before serving.
Enjoy the energy balls as a nutritious evening snack.

name: Green Tea with Ginger
instructions: Boil 250 ml of water in a kettle or saucepan.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, remove it from heat.
Add 1 tsp of green tea leaves and 0.5 tsp of grated ginger to the hot water.
Cover the mixture and let it steep for about 5 minutes.
After steeping, strain the tea into a cup to remove the leaves and ginger.
Enjoy your green tea with ginger as a soothing evening snack.

name: Light Bhel Puri
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 40 g of puffed rice with 20 g of finely chopped onion and 20 g of diced tomato.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon over the mixture.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp of chaat masala evenly over the ingredients.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until well mixed.
Serve the light bhel puri immediately as an evening snack.

name: Masala Makhana in Ghee
instructions: Heat 1 tsp of ghee in a pan over medium heat.
Add 30 g of makhana to the pan and roast them for about 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently until they become crisp.
Sprinkle 0.25 tsp of black pepper and 0.5 tsp of cumin powder over the roasted makhana.
Continue to roast the makhana for an additional 2-3 minutes to allow the spices to blend well.
Remove the pan from heat and let the masala makhana cool slightly before serving as an evening snack.

name: Masala Roasted Papad
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Take 1 piece of papad and place it on a baking tray.
Finely chop 20 g of onion and 20 g of tomato.
Spread the chopped onion and tomato evenly over the papad.
Sprinkle 1 tbsp of chopped coriander leaves on top of the vegetables.
Place the baking tray in the preheated oven and roast for about 5-7 minutes, or until the papad is crispy and golden.
Remove the tray from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.
Cut the masala roasted papad into wedges and serve as an evening snack.

name: Ragi Jaggery Cookies (Baked)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a mixing bowl, combine 50 g of Ragi Flour and 0.25 tsp of Cardamom.
In a separate bowl, melt 2 tsp of Ghee and mix in 20 g of Jaggery until well combined.
Pour the melted Ghee and Jaggery mixture into the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Shape the dough into small balls and flatten them slightly before placing them on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake the cookies in the preheated oven for about 15-20 minutes or until they are golden brown.
Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool on a wire rack before serving as an evening snack.

name: Roasted Chana with Jaggery
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 30 g of roasted chana with 15 g of jaggery, breaking the jaggery into smaller pieces if necessary.
Add 0.25 tsp of cardamom to the mixture and stir well to ensure even distribution of flavors.
Allow the mixture to sit for a few minutes to let the jaggery slightly melt and coat the roasted chana.
Serve the roasted chana with jaggery and cardamom in a small bowl as an evening snack.

name: Sabudana Kheer with Jaggery
instructions: Rinse 30 g of tapioca pearls under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak them in water for about 30 minutes.
In a saucepan, bring 200 ml of milk to a gentle boil over medium heat.
Once the milk is boiling, add the soaked tapioca pearls to the saucepan and stir well.
Cook the mixture on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the tapioca pearls become translucent, which should take about 10-15 minutes.
Add 15 g of jaggery to the kheer and stir until it completely dissolves.
Finally, add 0.25 tsp of cardamom to the kheer for flavor and mix well.
Remove the kheer from heat and let it cool slightly before serving.
Serve the sabudana kheer warm or chilled as an evening snack.

name: Bharli Vangi with Bhakri
instructions: Wash and dry the 150 g of brinjal, then make a slit lengthwise in each brinjal to create a pocket for stuffing.
In a pan, dry roast 20 g of peanuts until they are golden brown, then let them cool and grind them coarsely.
In the same pan, dry roast 1 tsp of sesame seeds until they are fragrant, then remove and set aside.
Mix the ground peanuts, roasted sesame seeds, and 5 g of jaggery in a bowl to create the stuffing for the brinjals.
Stuff each brinjal with the peanut and sesame mixture, ensuring they are well filled.
Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat and place the stuffed brinjals in it, cooking until they are tender and slightly charred, turning occasionally.
In a separate bowl, mix 80 g of bajra flour with water to form a smooth dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a flat disc to make bhakri.
Cook the bhakri on a hot tava until both sides are golden brown and cooked through.
Serve the bharli vangi hot with the bhakri for a delicious lunch.

name: Bhindi Sabji with Jowar Bhakri
instructions: Wash and trim the 150 g of okra, then cut them into small pieces.
Finely chop the 40 g of onion.
Heat a pan over medium heat and add 0.5 tsp of cumin seeds, allowing them to sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the chopped onion to the pan and sauté until they turn translucent.
Stir in the okra pieces and cook for about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle in 0.5 tsp of turmeric powder and mix well, cooking for an additional 5 minutes until the okra is tender.
In a separate bowl, mix 80 g of jowar flour with water to form a smooth dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a flat circle to form bhakris.
Cook the bhakris on a hot tava or skillet for about 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Serve the bhindi sabji hot with the jowar bhakris for lunch.

name: Chana Dal with Rice
instructions: Rinse 80 g of Chana Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for at least 30 minutes.
In a pot, add 100 g of Rice and 200 ml of water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 15 minutes until the rice is cooked and water is absorbed.
In a separate pan, heat a tablespoon of oil over medium heat and add 40 g of finely chopped Onion, sautéing until golden brown.
Add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds to the onions and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in 0.5 tsp of Turmeric Powder and the soaked Chana Dal, mixing well to combine.
Add enough water to cover the Chana Dal, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 30-40 minutes until the dal is tender.
Once the Chana Dal is cooked, season with salt to taste and serve hot alongside the cooked Rice.

name: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
instructions: Cook 100 g of rice according to package instructions until soft and fluffy.
Allow the cooked rice to cool to room temperature.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled rice with 100 g of low-fat curd and mix well until the rice is evenly coated.
In a small pan, heat a teaspoon of oil over medium heat.
Add 0.5 tsp of mustard seeds to the hot oil and let them splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves and 2 g of finely chopped ginger to the pan, sautéing for a minute until fragrant.
Pour the tempering mixture over the rice and curd mixture, stirring gently to combine.
Serve the curd rice chilled or at room temperature for lunch.

name: Dal Palak with Chapati
instructions: Rinse 60 g of Toor Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Toor Dal with enough water to cover it and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until the dal is soft, about 20-25 minutes.
While the dal is cooking, wash and chop 60 g of Spinach finely.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds. Sauté until they start to crackle.
Add 2 pieces of minced Garlic to the pan and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the chopped Spinach and cook until wilted, then mix this into the cooked Toor Dal. Season with salt to taste and simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
To make the Chapati, combine 80 g of Whole Wheat Flour with water to form a soft dough. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle on a floured surface.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook each Chapati until golden brown on both sides, puffing them up as they cook.
Serve the Dal Palak hot with the freshly made Chapati for a delicious lunch.

name: Dal Tadka with Steamed Rice
instructions: Rinse 80 g of Toor Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Toor Dal with 3 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until the dal is soft, about 20-25 minutes.
While the dal is cooking, rinse 100 g of Basmati Rice under cold water until the water runs clear.

In a separate pot, add the rinsed Basmati Rice with 2 cups of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for about 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy and water is absorbed.
In a small pan, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat. Add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Finely chop 2 pieces of Garlic and add them to the pan, sautéing until they turn golden brown.
Once the dal is cooked, add the sautéed garlic and cumin mixture to the dal, stirring well to combine.
Serve the hot Dal Tadka alongside the steamed Basmati Rice on a plate.

name: Egg Bhurji with Bhakri
instructions: Finely chop the 40g of onion and 40g of tomato, and slice the 1 green chilli.
In a pan, heat a little oil over medium heat and add the chopped onion, sautéing until translucent.
Add the chopped tomato and green chilli to the pan, cooking until the tomato softens.
Crack the 2 eggs into the pan, stirring continuously to scramble them with the onion and tomato mixture until fully cooked.
In a separate bowl, mix 80g of bajra flour with water to form a smooth dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a flat disc to form bhakris.
Cook the bhakris on a hot tava or skillet, flipping until both sides are golden brown and cooked through.
Serve the egg bhurji hot with the freshly made bhakris.

name: Gobi Matar with Chapati
instructions: Begin by washing and cutting the 120 g of cauliflower into small florets.
In a pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of cumin seeds, allowing them to sizzle.
Add the cauliflower florets to the pan and sauté for about 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Chop the 50 g of tomato and add it to the pan, cooking until it breaks down and combines with the cauliflower.
Stir in 50 g of green peas and cook for an additional 3-4 minutes until everything is well mixed and heated through.
In a separate bowl, combine 80 g of whole wheat flour with water to form a soft dough for the chapati.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Cook the rolled chapatis on a hot skillet for about 1-2 minutes on each side until they are golden brown.
Serve the Gobi Matar hot alongside the freshly made chapatis for a delicious lunch.

name: Kala Chana Curry with Rice
instructions: Soak 80 g of Kala Chana in water overnight, then drain and rinse before cooking.
In a pot, add the soaked Kala Chana with enough water to cover them and cook until tender, about 30-40 minutes.
While the Kala Chana is cooking, rinse 100 g of Rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a separate pot, bring 200 ml of water to a boil, add the rinsed Rice, and cook covered on low heat for about 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed.
Finely chop 40 g of Onion and 50 g of Tomato.
In a pan, heat a little oil and sauté the chopped Onion until golden brown.
Add the chopped Tomato to the pan and cook until soft, then stir in 0.5 tsp of Garam Masala.
Once the Kala Chana is cooked, drain any excess water and add them to the pan with the onion and tomato mixture, stirring well to combine.
Serve the Kala Chana curry hot alongside the cooked Rice.

name: Kerala Fish Curry with Rice
instructions: Rinse 100 g of basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of mustard seeds, allowing them to splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves to the pan and sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add 120 g of fish to the pan and cook until it is lightly browned on all sides.
Grate 40 g of coconut and add it to the pan, mixing well with the fish and spices.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to a pot with double the amount of water, bringing it to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the rice cook for about 15 minutes or until tender.
Serve the fish curry hot alongside the cooked basmati rice.

name: Lauki Kofta in Tomato Gravy
instructions: Grate the 120 g of Doodhi (Bottle Gourd) and squeeze out excess moisture.
In a mixing bowl, combine the grated Doodhi with 30 g of Chickpea Flour (Besan) and mix well to form a dough-like consistency.
Shape the mixture into small balls to form the koftas.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the koftas until they are golden brown on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In another pan, heat a little oil and add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds, allowing them to splutter.
Chop the 80 g of Tomato and add it to the pan, cooking until it softens and releases its juices.
Blend the cooked tomatoes into a smooth gravy and return it to the pan, simmering for a few minutes.
Add the fried koftas to the tomato gravy and let them soak in the flavors for a couple of minutes.
Garnish with 10 g of Cashews, chopped if desired, and serve hot with rice or roti for lunch.

name: Lemon Rice with Peanuts
instructions: Rinse 100 g of rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it for 20 minutes.
In a pot, bring 200 ml of water to a boil and add the soaked rice.
Cover and simmer the rice on low heat for about 15 minutes, or until all the water is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
While the rice is cooking, heat a small pan over medium heat and add 15 g of peanuts.
Toast the peanuts for about 3-4 minutes until they are golden brown, then remove them from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add 0.5 tsp of mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add 5 pieces of curry leaves to the pan and sauté for a minute until fragrant.
Once the rice is cooked, fluff it with a fork and add the mustard seeds and curry leaves mixture.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon over the rice and mix well.
Finally, add the toasted peanuts, stir gently, and serve the lemon rice warm for lunch.

name: Masoor Dal Khichdi
instructions: Rinse 50 g of Masoor Dal and 50 g of Rice together under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a pot, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat.
Add 0.5 tsp of Cumin Seeds to the hot Ghee and sauté until they start to crackle.
Peel and chop 40 g of Carrot into small pieces, then add them to the pot and sauté for a few minutes until slightly softened.
Add the rinsed Masoor Dal and Rice to the pot, stirring well to combine with the carrots and spices.
Pour in enough water to cover the mixture by about an inch, then bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for about 20 minutes or until the dal and rice are cooked through and the mixture is creamy.
Remove from heat and let it sit covered for a few minutes before serving.

name: Methi Matar Cashew Gravy
instructions: Begin by finely chopping the 40 g of onion and set it aside.
In a pan, heat a small amount of oil and sauté the chopped onion until it becomes translucent.
Add the 5 g of finely grated ginger to the pan and sauté for another minute until fragrant.
Next, add the 60 g of green peas to the pan and cook for a few minutes until they are tender.
Stir in the 60 g of fenugreek leaves and cook until they wilt down.
In a separate small pan, lightly roast the 15 g of cashews until they are golden brown, then chop them coarsely.
Combine the roasted cashews into the pan with the vegetables and mix well.
Season the mixture with salt to taste and let it simmer for a few minutes to blend the flavors.
Serve the Methi Matar Cashew Gravy hot, garnished with the remaining cashews if desired.

name: Palak Paneer with Chapati
instructions: Wash the 100 g of spinach thoroughly and blanch it in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and cool it in ice water.
In a blender, combine the blanched spinach, 50 g of chopped tomato, and 5 g of ginger to create a smooth paste.
In a pan, heat a little oil and add the spinach mixture, cooking it for about 5 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Cut the 80 g of low-fat paneer into cubes and add it to the spinach mixture, gently stirring to combine.
Cook the palak paneer for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the paneer to absorb the flavors.
In a bowl, combine 80 g of whole wheat flour with water to form a soft dough for the chapati.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a tawa or skillet and cook each chapati for about 1 minute on each side until golden brown and puffed up.
Serve the palak paneer hot alongside the freshly made chapati.

name: Pithla Bhakri
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 60 g of Chickpea Flour (Besan) with 0.5 tsp of Turmeric Powder.
Add water gradually to the flour mixture, stirring continuously until you achieve a smooth batter.
In a pan, heat some oil over medium heat and sauté 40 g of finely chopped Onion until translucent.
Add 3 g of minced Garlic to the pan and sauté for another minute until fragrant.
Pour the chickpea flour batter into the pan with the onions and garlic, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cook the mixture on low heat for about 5-7 minutes, until it thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
While the Pithla is cooking, prepare the Bhakri by mixing 80 g of Jowar Flour with water to form a dough.
Divide the dough into small balls, flatten them into discs, and cook on a hot tava until both sides are golden brown.
Serve the Pithla hot with the freshly made Bhakri for a delicious lunch.

name: Tawa Pulao
instructions: Rinse 100 g of Basmati Rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pan, heat 1 tsp of Ghee over medium heat.
Add the soaked and drained Basmati Rice to the pan and sauté for 2-3 minutes until the rice is slightly translucent.
Add 80 g of Mixed Vegetables to the pan and stir well to combine with the rice.
Chop 50 g of Tomato and add it to the pan, mixing it in with the rice and vegetables.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp of Pav Bhaji Masala over the mixture and stir to evenly coat the ingredients.

Pour in enough water to cover the rice and vegetables, bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let it cook for about 15 minutes or until the rice is fully cooked and the water is absorbed.
Once cooked, fluff the Tawa Pulao gently with a fork and serve hot for lunch.

name: Vegetable Biryani with Raita
instructions: Rinse 120 g of Basmati Rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 30 minutes.
In a pot, bring 2 cups of water to a boil, add the soaked Basmati Rice, and cook until the rice is 70% done, about 10 minutes.
Drain the partially cooked rice and set it aside.
In the same pot, add 100 g of Mixed Vegetables and sauté for a few minutes until they are tender.
Stir in 0.5 tsp of Garam Masala and mix well with the vegetables.
Layer the partially cooked Basmati Rice over the sautéed vegetables, cover the pot, and cook on low heat for another 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
While the biryani is cooking, prepare the raita by finely chopping 40 g of Cucumber and mixing it with 50 g of Low-Fat Curd in a bowl.
Once the biryani is done, fluff it gently with a fork and serve it hot with the cucumber raita on the side.

name: Vegetable Korma with Pulka
instructions: In a pan, lightly roast the 10 g of cashews until golden brown, then set aside.
In the same pan, add the 120 g of mixed vegetables and sauté until they are tender.
Add the 30 g of coconut and the 2 pieces of cardamom to the pan, stirring well to combine with the vegetables.
Cook the mixture for a few more minutes until the coconut is fragrant, then remove from heat.
In a bowl, combine the 80 g of whole wheat flour with water to form a soft dough for the pulka.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each ball into a thin circle.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook each pulka for about 1-2 minutes on each side until puffed and lightly browned.
Serve the vegetable korma hot, garnished with the roasted cashews, alongside the freshly made pulka.

name: Whole Masoor Dal with Rice
instructions: Rinse 80 g of Whole Masoor Dal under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 30 minutes.
In a pot, add the soaked Whole Masoor Dal with 400 ml of water and bring it to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer the dal for about 30-40 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
While the dal is cooking, rinse 100 g of Rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a separate pot, add the rinsed Rice with 200 ml of water and a pinch of salt, then bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook the Rice for about 15 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
Finely chop 40 g of Onion and 50 g of Tomato, and grate 5 g of Ginger.
In a pan, heat a little oil and sauté the chopped Onion until translucent, then add the grated Ginger and chopped Tomato, cooking until the tomato softens.
Once the dal is cooked, mix in the sautéed onion, ginger, and tomato mixture, and let it simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
Serve the Whole Masoor Dal hot alongside the cooked Rice for a wholesome lunch.

name: Ajwain and Jeera Water
instructions: In a small bowl, combine 0.5 tsp of Ajwain and 1 tsp of Cumin Seeds.
Add 250 ml of water to the bowl with the spices.
Bring the mixture to a boil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Once boiling, reduce the heat and let it simmer for about 5 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat and allow the water to cool slightly.
Strain the water into a glass to remove the spices.
Drink the Ajwain and Jeera water warm in the morning for best results.

name: Amla and Honey Tonic
instructions: In a glass, combine 30 ml of Amla Juice with 200 ml of Water.
Add 1 tsp of Honey to the mixture.
Stir the mixture well until the honey is fully dissolved.
Drink the tonic in the morning for optimal benefits.

name: Ashwagandha Warm Milk
instructions: In a small saucepan, pour 200 ml of milk and heat it over medium heat until it is warm but not boiling.
Once the milk is warm, add 0.5 tsp of Ashwagandha powder and 0.25 tsp of cardamom to the milk.
Whisk the mixture gently to ensure that the Ashwagandha powder and cardamom are well combined with the milk.
Continue to heat the mixture for another minute, stirring occasionally, to enhance the flavors.
Remove the saucepan from heat and pour the warm milk into a cup.
Enjoy your Ashwagandha warm milk as a soothing morning drink.

name: Brahmi Capsule
instructions: Take 1 Brahmi Capsule with a glass of water after breakfast.

name: CCF Tea (Cumin-Coriander-Fennel)
instructions: In a small pan, add 1 tsp of cumin seeds, 1 tsp of coriander seeds, and 1 tsp of fennel seeds.
Toast the seeds over medium heat for about 2-3 minutes until they become fragrant, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Once toasted, add 250 ml of water to the pan with the seeds.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 5-7 minutes.
After simmering, remove the pan from heat and strain the tea into a cup to remove the seeds.
Enjoy your CCF tea warm in the morning.

name: Chyawanprash
instructions: Take 1 tsp of Chyawanprash.
Consume it with a glass of warm water or milk.
Enjoy it in the morning for best results.

name: Ginger Lemon Warm Water
instructions: Boil 250 ml of water in a kettle or pot.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, remove it from heat.
Add 1 tsp of grated ginger to the hot water.
Squeeze the juice from half a lemon into the water, ensuring to remove any seeds.
Stir the mixture well to combine the ginger and lemon juice.
Let the drink steep for about 5 minutes to enhance the flavors.
Strain the mixture into a cup to remove the ginger pieces.
Enjoy your warm ginger lemon water in the morning.

name: Guduchi Giloy Tablet
instructions: Take 1 piece of Giloy Tablet with a glass of water in the morning.

name: Kokum Sharbat
instructions: Soak 2 pieces of kokum in 250 ml of water for about 30 minutes until they soften.
After soaking, mash the kokum in the water to extract the juice.
Strain the mixture to remove the kokum pulp, leaving a clear liquid.
Add 10 g of jaggery to the strained kokum juice and stir until fully dissolved.
Mix in 0.25 tsp of cumin powder for added flavor.
Serve the kokum sharbat chilled or at room temperature in a glass.

name: Lemongrass Tea
instructions: Begin by washing the 2 pieces of lemongrass thoroughly to remove any dirt or impurities.
Using a knife, gently crush the lemongrass pieces to release their essential oils.
In a pot, bring 250 ml of water to a boil over medium heat.
Once the water is boiling, add the crushed lemongrass pieces to the pot.
Reduce the heat and let the mixture simmer for about 5-10 minutes to infuse the flavors.
After simmering, remove the pot from heat and strain the tea into a cup to remove the lemongrass pieces.
Serve the lemongrass tea hot, and enjoy it as a refreshing morning drink.

name: Methi Soaked Water
instructions: In a clean glass, add 1 tsp of fenugreek seeds.
Pour 250 ml of water over the fenugreek seeds.
Cover the glass and let it soak overnight.
In the morning, stir the mixture well.
Strain the water into another glass, discarding the seeds.
Your methi soaked water is ready to drink.
Consume it on an empty stomach for best results.

name: Moringa Leaf Tea
instructions: Boil 250 ml of water in a kettle or pot.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, add 5 pieces of Moringa Leaves to the water.
Reduce the heat and let the Moringa Leaves steep in the hot water for about 5-7 minutes.
After steeping, strain the tea into a cup to remove the Moringa Leaves.
Squeeze the juice of 0.25 piece of Lemon into the tea for added flavor.
Stir well and enjoy your Moringa Leaf Tea in the morning.

name: Pomegranate Beetroot Juice
instructions: Wash the pomegranate and beetroot thoroughly under running water.
Cut the beetroot into small pieces to facilitate blending.
Remove the seeds from the pomegranate and set them aside.
In a blender, combine the pomegranate seeds, beetroot pieces, and 100 ml of water.
Blend the mixture until smooth and well combined.
Strain the blended mixture through a fine sieve or cheesecloth into a glass to remove any pulp.
Serve the pomegranate beetroot juice immediately in a chilled glass for a refreshing morning drink.

name: Sabja Basil Seed Water
instructions: Soak 1 tsp of basil seeds in 250 ml of water for about 30 minutes until they swell and become gelatinous.
Squeeze the juice of 0.5 piece of lemon into the soaked basil seeds and water mixture.
Stir the mixture well to combine the lemon juice with the basil seeds and water.
Serve the sabja basil seed water in a glass and enjoy it as a refreshing morning drink.

name: Shatavari Capsule
instructions: Take 1 Shatavari Capsule with a glass of water after breakfast.

name: Wheatgrass Juice with Lemon
instructions: Squeeze the juice from half a lemon into a glass.
Add 30 ml of wheatgrass juice to the glass.
Pour in 200 ml of water.
Stir the mixture well until combined.
Serve immediately and enjoy your refreshing wheatgrass juice with lemon in the morning.

name: Ajwain Digestive Water
instructions: Boil 200 ml of water in a pot.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, add 0.5 tsp of ajwain.
Reduce the heat and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove the pot from heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly.
Strain the liquid into a glass, discarding the ajwain seeds.
Drink the ajwain water warm before bedtime.

name: Ashwagandha Capsule
instructions: Take 1 Ashwagandha Capsule with a glass of water before bedtime.

name: Ashwagandha Nutmeg Milk
instructions: In a small saucepan, pour 200 ml of Milk.
Add 0.5 tsp of Ashwagandha Powder to the milk.
Sprinkle in 0.1 tsp of Nutmeg.
Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring gently until warm, but do not bring it to a boil.
Once warmed, remove from heat and let it cool slightly.
Pour the Ashwagandha Nutmeg Milk into a cup.
Enjoy your drink before bedtime for a calming effect.

name: Brahmi Shankhpushpi Tea
instructions: Boil 250 ml of water in a saucepan.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, add 0.5 tsp of Brahmi and 0.5 tsp of Shankhpushpi.
Reduce the heat and let the mixture simmer for about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat and strain the tea into a cup.
Allow the tea to cool slightly before drinking it at night.

name: Chamomile Tea with Honey
instructions: Let the tea cool slightly after boiling before stirring in the honey - do not add honey while the liquid is hot.

name: Mulethi Licorice Tea
instructions: Boil 250 ml of water in a saucepan.
Once the water reaches a rolling boil, add 1 tsp of Licorice Root.
Reduce the heat and let it simmer for about 5-10 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat and strain the tea into a cup.
Allow the tea to cool slightly before drinking, and enjoy it as a soothing night drink.

name: Saffron Cardamom Milk (Kesar)
instructions: In a small saucepan, heat 200 ml of milk over low heat until it is warm but not boiling.
Add 3 pieces of saffron to the warm milk and stir gently to infuse the flavor.
Crush 0.25 tsp of cardamom and add it to the milk, stirring well to combine.
Allow the mixture to simmer on low heat for about 5 minutes, letting the flavors meld together.
Remove the saucepan from heat and let the milk cool slightly before serving.
Pour the saffron cardamom milk into a cup and enjoy it warm as a night drink.

name: Shatavari Milk
instructions: In a small saucepan, pour 200 ml of milk and heat it gently over low flame until warm, but not boiling.
Add 0.5 tsp of Shatavari powder to the warm milk and stir well to combine.
Incorporate 0.25 tsp of cardamom into the mixture, stirring until fully dissolved.
Continue to heat the mixture for another minute, ensuring it is warm and well blended.
Pour the Shatavari milk into a cup and allow it to cool slightly before drinking.
Enjoy the Shatavari milk as a soothing night drink before bedtime.

name: Triphala Tablet
instructions: Take 1 piece of Triphala Tablet with a glass of water before bedtime.

name: Warm Almond Milk with Saffron
instructions: Pour 200 ml of almond milk into a small saucepan.
Add 3 pieces of saffron to the almond milk.
Sprinkle in 0.25 tsp of cardamom.
Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring gently until warm, but do not bring it to a boil.
Once warmed, remove from heat and let it steep for a couple of minutes to enhance the flavors.
Strain the mixture into a cup to remove the saffron strands.
Serve warm as a soothing night drink.
